basics.name: Kenneth Browder
basics.label: Master's student, MIT Media Lab
basics.summary: Kenneth Browder is a master's student in the Viral Communications group at the MIT Media Lab, with a background in graphics, physical simulation, and generative AI. His work focuses on creative and fun uses of technology that help people see themselves and others in new ways. Ken is always interested to hear from artists, researchers, and builders about new creative projects that help humans express themselves and understand each other.

work.name: MIT Media Lab, Viral Communications
work.summary: Graduate research assistant advised by Andy Lippman.

work.name: PixAI
highlights: Built much of the frontend and backend of PixAI's conversational creative assistant: brief planning, parallel creative directions with live streaming, batch generation, and brand house styles with a moodboard editor.
Led a platform redesign from Figma through implementation, and designed an editor application that unifies separate workflows into one photo-editor-style tool.
R&D: evaluated state-of-the-art generative models and integrated them into the product.
Prototyped a reference-free eye-measurement tool that combines several models to measure IPD and other facial dimensions without a scale reference.

work.name: Human-Computer Interaction Institute, Carnegie Mellon University
work.summary: Built a design tool for self-actuated metamaterial mechanisms (SVG motion paths to cell layouts, with physical simulation) and validated it on 3D-printed, Arduino-actuated prototypes.
